conventions: Where kol carries a pronominal suffix (kullekem, kullam) and the ASV writes one subject pronoun for the finite verb of that clause and nothing but all for the quantifier, the pronoun is the finite verb's under rule 17 and the suffix is the unrendered occurrence under rule 22: JOS.8.4 be ye all ready and JOS.8.24 they were all fallen both put the pronoun on the verb. Rule 19's of-plus-pronoun unit needs a written of, and its bare-pronoun sentence governs a pronoun written in the quantifier phrase's own place; rule 18's subject-pronoun case reaches a suffix on an infinitive construct, which is why JOS.8.24's until they were consumed keeps its they on tummam. BSB represents both suffixes, and that is the documented convention difference rather than evidence against this reading.

Which morpheme bears a presentative there was is decided by which side of the Hebrew clause is the predicate, not by the English frame: a prepositional predicate takes it (JOS.8.11 benayw, there was ... between, rule 49), a predicative participle takes it while the preposition beside it keeps its own word (JOS.8.14 orev lo, there was an ambush against him, rule 20), and a finite verb takes it wherever one stands (JOS.8.17 nishar, there was not a man left, rule 17). Read the clause before placing the dummy; the three shapes recur across the chapter and are not a split.
report: Checked all 73 candidate lemma groups and read the dump end to end for the added units the table is blind to (7: JOS.8.11 even and men, JOS.8.13 that, JOS.8.14 it, JOS.8.25 even, JOS.8.28 even, JOS.8.31 man). Two genuine splits found; both patched.

Split 1 (JOS.8.7 against JOS.8.8): both clauses write an object marker on a noun the English verb reaches through a preposition - take possession OF the city, seized UPON the city. JOS.8.8 gave the word to the marker; JOS.8.7 gave it to the verb's rendering and left the marker unrepresented. Rule 44's limit (a present marker takes the word before a supplied reading) and rule 16's first family settle it for the marker, and rule 16's subtraction test agrees: dropping of leaves take possession whole and removes only the object relation. The corpus aligns a To marker to of in 82 units. JOS.8.7 patched; JOS.8.8 stands.

Split 2 (JOS.8.24 against JOS.8.4): kol plus a pronominal suffix beside a finite verb for which the ASV writes one subject pronoun. JOS.8.4 (be ye all ready) gave ye to the verb and left the suffix of kullekem unrepresented; JOS.8.24 (they were all fallen) gave they to the suffix of kullam. I kept the verb reading and patched JOS.8.24: English requires a subject for the finite verb while kol keeps its own all, so the subtraction test finds it is the verb's rendering that fails without the pronoun, and rule 17's permission is what the rest of the chapter applies in dozens of units. The competing reading (rule 19's bare-pronoun sentence sending it to the suffix under rule 18) is named in the unit note. The infinitive-construct suffix of tummam in the same verse keeps its own they under rule 18, which is a different case and unchanged.

Checked and found consistent, licensed by the source or by what the ASV wrote: the hayah presentative frame and where its that falls (8.5, 8.14 and 8.24 give it to the written apodosis waw, 8.8 keeps it on the verb because that apodosis writes no waw, per rule 45); appositional even (the marker stands on the appositive in 8.13 and takes it, while 8.11, 8.25 and 8.28 mark it added because the clause's marker stands elsewhere or nowhere); the bein pairs of 8.9, 8.11 and 8.12; the fusions lifney, liqrat, kaasher, ad asher, meaharey, betokh, beqerev, el mul and aharey ken, each headed as rules 23 and 30 direct; wherein at 8.24 as a three-morpheme fusion against upon which at 8.31 split with the suffix unrepresented, which the ASV's one word against two licenses; article handling on the name Ai and in arthrous chains (rules 29, 41, 47); supplied directional prepositions given to the goal noun (8.1, 8.3, 8.10, 8.19, 8.20, 8.24) under rule 33; and the light-verb heads (arose up early, rose up early, drew nigh, made an end, took for prey, lie in ambush).

Presentative there was is borne by three different morphemes in this chapter and each is licensed by which side the Hebrew makes the predicate: the preposition at 8.11 (bein, rule 49), the predicative participle at 8.14 (orev, rule 20) with the lamed keeping its own against, and the finite verb at 8.17 (nishar, rule 17). Recorded as a convention rather than patched.

BSB: no genuine error. The Td (22), To (5), R (8) and Rd (6) disagreements are the documented convention difference - the ASV writes no word for those morphemes in its recastings, and BSB attaches them to their phrase. JOS.8.4 kem and JOS.8.31 hen are the two where BSB's representation is the alternative reading rejected above and under rule 22, and JOS.8.20 waw is the apodosis waw the ASV leaves unrendered. No accepted edge was changed to improve the rate.

No promotion. The kol-suffix judgment would be a useful amendment to rule 19's bare-pronoun sentence, but the precedent supplied gives no count for that exact shape, and a rule the corpus might contradict is worse than none, so it is recorded as a chapter convention instead.
